summary: - _(b) Pass appropriate orders/directions reviewing the Order dated 08.02.2023 passed by this Hon’ble Commission in Petition No. 252/MP/2021 thereby referring the dispute to arbitration._ - a. The Review Petitioner filed Petition No. 252/MP/2021 for referring a dispute between the Review Petitioner and Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), Respondent No. 4, to arbitral proceedings under Section 79(1)(f) of the Act and to appoint an Arbitral Tribunal in terms of Section 158 of the Act. h. In terms of the liberty granted by the Hon’ble Punjab and Haryana High Court, the Review Petitioner approached the Commission seeking reference of the dispute between the Review Petitioner and BBMB to arbitration. However, the Commission erroneously dismissed the said petition _inter alia_ holding that the dispute raised does not pertain to the tariff and the Commission does not have jurisdiction. - a. The Commission erroneously held that the dispute raised in the original petition does not pertain to the tariff by ignoring the following facts: b. Section 79(1)(f) of the Act provides for adjudication of a dispute by the Commission involving a generating company. The original petition was filed invoking Section 79(1)(f) of the Act, wherein the Review Petitioner raised a dispute with BBMB regarding an excess payment made to BBMB for the electricity supplied by it. However, this aspect was disregarded, and it was erroneously held that the dispute is not amenable to adjudicatory jurisdiction under Section 79(1)(f) of the Act. In this regard, the Review Petitioner again placed reliance on the APTEL’s judgment in Appeal Nos. 94 and 95 of 2012. 6. The Review Petitioner, in its written submissions dated 25.9.2025, reiterated that the Review Petitioner raised a tariff dispute in the original petition. However, the Commission in the impugned order treated the issue as one pertaining to the pilferage of electricity and erroneously dismissed the petition. The Review Petitioner has submitted that the Review Petitioner sought reference of a dispute qua payments made to BBMB in excess of the tariff agreed for the purchase of power, i.e., payments were remitted more than the actual power consumed by the State of Haryana. The power to regulate tariffs also includes the power to effect recovery/ reconciliation of excess payments made to the tariff generator. The Review Petitioner has further submitted that the original petition did not involve the adjudication of the issue of pilferage of electricity at the 66 kV Sub-station of BBMB. The Review Petitioner also submitted that the Commission overlooked certain aspects while passing the impugned order, and it resulted in an error apparent on the face of the record, and it is a fit case for the exercise of review jurisdiction by the Commission. 8. The basic contention of the Review Petitioner is that the Review Petitioner had paid for the power that Bhushan Industries pilfered from the BBMB Chandigarh 66 kV Substation with the connivance of officials of the Electricity Department, Chandigarh and BBMB. Therefore, the Review Petitioner requested BBMB to refund the amount paid for the power that was not consumed by it, i.e. the power which Bhushan Industries pilfered. However, there was no response from BBMB. Accordingly, HVPNL filed Petition No.252/MP/2021 for referring the dispute to arbitration in terms of Section 79(1)(f) of the Act. Section 79(1)(f) of the Act provides for adjudication of a dispute involving a generating company, and the said section was invoked in the main petition for adjudication of the dispute in respect of the excess payment made to BBMB. However, the Commission in the impugned order erroneously dismissed the said petition, considering it as an issue pertaining to pilferage. 10. In short, the Review Petitioner’s contention is that the Commission erroneously held that the nature of the dispute raised does not pertain to tariff, and it is in respect of pilferage of power and concluded that it does not have the jurisdiction to deal with disputes pertaining to pilferage of power. 11. We have considered the submissions of the Review Petitioner. The Commission has dealt in detail with the nature of the dispute raised and its jurisdiction to deal with the dispute in the impugned order dated 8.2.2023. Further, the Commission considered the APTEL’s Appeal Nos. 94 and 95 of 2012 in the impugned order, which was relied upon by the Review Petitioner in the main petition. The relevant portion of the order dated _adjudicate the dispute or refer the dispute to arbitrator or arbitrators appointed by it. Since we have come to the conclusion in this order that the present dispute is not amenable to adjudicatory jurisdiction under Section 79(1)(f) of the Act, the question of reference of the dispute to arbitration does not arise._ ” 14. In view of the above discussion, we are of the view that the Review Petitioner’s contention that the dispute raised is regarding non-refund of the excess amount paid by the Review Petitioner to BBMB and that the Commission has the power to refer the same
title: Review Petition under Section 94(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 103 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 1999 along with the applicable provisions of law, seeking review of the order dated 8.2.2023 in Petition No. 252/MP/2021. Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited
